key_insight: Machine learning can accurately predict and optimize the strength and hardness of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints from a few welding parameters.
engineering_relevance: The approach helps engineers select welding settings that improve joint quality faster than trial-and-error experimentation, supporting smarter and more sustainable process design.
method: Used TRS, TTS, and TPD as inputs to predict UTS and micro-hardness.
Trained and compared LR, RF, SVR, XGBoost, and KNN on an 80:20 train-test split.
Evaluated models with MAE, RMSE, RAE, and RRSE to identify the best predictors.
evidence_signal: Random Forest gave the best UTS prediction on the test set (MAE 9.007 MPa, RMSE 12.975 MPa), while SVR with an RBF kernel was best for micro-hardness (MAE 0.923 HV, RMSE 1.155 HV).
watch_item: Model reliability may be limited by the size and range of the experimental dataset, so performance should be revalidated before use on different alloys or welding setups.
paper_title: Explainable machine learning approach for predicting mechanical characteristics of AA6082–AA7075 friction stir welded joints
